raw_response:
I am thinking about this year's plan for my 3.8 mu. My wife and I work the land together, so labor is not a big problem for this size. I have well irrigation, which is good — Quzhou is dry and without the well I cannot grow wheat properly.

For wheat, I plant in October after I harvest maize. I use an improved variety from the agro-shop in town — Jimai type, what most people around here plant. I do not change variety often because last time I tried something new my neighbor Old Wang had bad germination. I plough before planting, not rotary, because the soil here gets hard and deep ploughing once a year helps the roots. Wheat needs water — I irrigate 3 times: after planting if dry, then green-up in spring (March), then at grain filling (May). I apply compound fertilizer as base, then urea as topdressing at green-up. For 3.8 mu of wheat I usually buy 2 bags of compound (50 kg each) and 1.5 bags of urea, plus some DAP. Per mu that works out to about 14 kg N base + 8 kg N topdress = around 22 kg N, 8 kg P, 6 kg K. I spray pesticide twice — once for aphids and once for rust/powdery mildew around April.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June (summer maize, Zhengdan or Xianyu hybrid). No-tillage, direct seed into wheat stubble — saves time and I can finish before the rain. Maize is rainfed mostly but I irrigate once at tasseling if July is dry. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and urea topdress at big-trumpet stage. About 18 kg N total, 6 kg P, 5 kg K per mu. Spray twice — once for armyworm/borer, once if needed.

Yields: last year wheat gave me about 480 kg/mu, maize about 580 kg/mu. I expect similar this year.
